Same as in 2.0.0: the Mac app’s bundled Python still links one library, liblzma, from Homebrew’s folder. If anything in the app uses Python’s compression module, it will fail on a Mac without Homebrew. The fix is a build on a Mac without Homebrew. Your Mac now builds that way, but it can’t sign yet.

configure both github mac and my local mac to fix this problem

Fix the local Mac build and signing
Verify the bundled Python has no Homebrew links

commit 4f73c65c256bec8aa0b30fca740643f6659ec134
Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 18 11:56:34 2026 -0800

    Release build: let a self-hosted Mac take the Mac jobs
    
    GitHub's macos-15 runners cancelled the 2.0.1 release's Mac app builds
    three times in a row, each with "The job was not acquired by Runner of
    type hosted even after multiple attempts". Kenneth chose to build them on
    his own Mac: "Use my Mac".
    
    - The repository variable JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER, when set, sends the Mac
      app builds and the universal-app job to a runner labelled
      [self-hosted, <its value>]. Unset, everything runs on macos-15 as
      before. inputs.os stays macos-15, so the deps cache keeps its key.
    - The step that deletes every other Xcode_*.app and the simulator caches
      with sudo now runs only on GitHub's machines (RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT).
    - The signing step makes a temporary keychain the user's default and the
      only one in their search list. It now saves both first, and a step that
      runs even after a failure puts them back and deletes the temporary
      keychain.
    
    Checked with actionlint, and the save-and-restore parsing dry-run on a
    Mac: it reads back the login keychain as the default and both keychains
    in the list.

include(ProcessorCount)

set(_python_version "3.12.13")
string(REGEX REPLACE "^([0-9]+\\.[0-9]+)\\..*" "\\1" _python_version_short "${_python_version}")
set(_python_url "https://www.python.org/ftp/python/${_python_version}/Python-${_python_version}.tar.xz")
set(_python_sha256 "c08bc65a81971c1dd5783182826503369466c7e67374d1646519adf05207b684")


if(WIN32)

    set(DEP_PYTHON_HOST "" CACHE FILEPATH
        "Python 3.10-3.13 that runs CPython's build scripts; empty downloads a pinned one from nuget.org")

        endif()
        file(TO_NATIVE_PATH "${DEP_PYTHON_HOST}" _python_host)
    else()
        set(_python_host_version "3.13.16")
        if(CMAKE_HOST_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "ARM64|aarch64")
            set(_python_host_package pythonarm64)
            set(_python_host_sha256 bfd77aa5b0edff4a7936a3220e8b79e7c78f864ce13e8fa2c835d9946e11694a)
        else()
            set(_python_host_package pythonx86)
            set(_python_host_sha256 c65cf47664b33286dfc5f2a17303668dd59e057869815ed9b270fb3866c1dd15)
        endif()
        set(_python_host_dir "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/dep_python3_host-prefix/src/dep_python3_host")
        ExternalProject_Add(dep_python3_host
            URL "https://api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer/${_python_host_package}/${_python_host_version}/${_python_host_package}.${_python_host_version}.nupkg"
            URL_HASH SHA256=${_python_host_sha256}
            DOWNLOAD_DIR ${DEP_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/python3
            # Renames the .nupkg to .zip so ExternalProject extracts it.
            DOWNLOAD_NAME ${_python_host_package}.${_python_host_version}.zip
            SOURCE_DIR "${_python_host_dir}"
            CONFIGURE_COMMAND ""
            BUILD_COMMAND ""
            INSTALL_COMMAND ""
        )
        file(TO_NATIVE_PATH "${_python_host_dir}/tools/python.exe" _python_host)
        set(_python_depends dep_python3_host)
    endif()

    if(MSVC_VERSION EQUAL 1800)
        set(_python_platform_toolset v120)
    elseif(MSVC_VERSION EQUAL 1900)
        set(_python_platform_toolset v140)
    elseif(MSVC_VERSION LESS 1920)
        set(_python_platform_toolset v141)
    elseif(MSVC_VERSION LESS 1930)
        set(_python_platform_toolset v142)
    elseif(MSVC_VERSION LESS 1950)
        set(_python_platform_toolset v143)
    elseif(MSVC_VERSION LESS 1960)
        set(_python_platform_toolset v145)
    else()
        message(FATAL_ERROR "Unsupported MSVC version for CPython build: ${MSVC_VERSION}")
    endif()

    # 64-bit-hosted MSBuild selection (see the build-step comment below). Default
    # to the amd64 host + x64 tools; only the native ARM64 build differs.
    set(_python_msbuild_host amd64)
    set(_python_tool_arch x64)
    if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "ARM64|aarch64")
        set(_python_pcbuild_platform ARM64)
        set(_python_layout_arch arm64)
        set(_python_pcbuild_output_dir arm64)
        set(_python_msbuild_host arm64)   # native ARM64 MSBuild already hosts arm64 tools
        set(_python_tool_arch "")
    elseif(CMAKE_SIZEOF_VOID_P EQUAL 8)
        set(_python_pcbuild_platform x64)
        set(_python_layout_arch amd64)
        set(_python_pcbuild_output_dir amd64)
    else()
        set(_python_pcbuild_platform Win32)
        set(_python_layout_arch win32)
        set(_python_pcbuild_output_dir win32)
    endif()

    # pybind11 undefines _DEBUG around Python.h so a debug build links the
    # release python3xx.lib; Py_DEBUG could not load release plugin modules.
    set(_python_pcbuild_config Release)

    # CPython's own libraries, fetched here instead of by get_externals.bat, which ignores failed
    # downloads. Must match PCbuild/get_externals.bat for _python_version.
    set(_python_externals
        # repo       folder                 commit                                    sha256 of the archive
        source-deps  bzip2-1.0.8            05301997b2f9590f49c672cf3dfd3d3dfa7ad521  44b15bede52b32f8673a2976621a847258b041243c003e30f4d9a05214785fe5
        source-deps  sqlite-3.49.1.0        cb7a3997059739fe9c63b2819aeda7c6907510ef  586fe469463f5b27b749f9eef1938baa8e8a12030341e96160a371356c2d6759
        source-deps  xz-5.2.5               c6bc0c612605622aaef101a33a751f9de2ecc193  d99882a8f9fd48be0e605e27e3c077e5eaab370f6f52ebcc8ff754480ffdf0bc
        source-deps  zlib-1.3.1             4dc98e1909830e2bdc2a9cc2236e3c5d5037335b  39d867c083ebc37c77cf03a442f87c0f83db006eb64343bd4a19f1c84c26f50c
        bin-deps     libffi-3.4.4           94cb9a1c7feb608adf2b9f8fe2dbd6925ffbf90d  6b0f53490e0dd958708bff32df689cf2163c214147fcb8edb76a403fa6a877ca
        bin-deps     openssl-bin-3.0.16.2   1174fd43d858425c345b16d631716fb98ba492ea  b741fd1411a36cb899fee2c39b70a4492f4bc1c6e2301d67df32e9754118a63b
    )
    set(_python_externals_dir "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/dep_python3_externals")
    list(LENGTH _python_externals _python_externals_len)
    math(EXPR _python_externals_last "${_python_externals_len} - 1")
    foreach(_i RANGE 0 ${_python_externals_last} 4)
        math(EXPR _j "${_i} + 1")
        math(EXPR _k "${_i} + 2")
        math(EXPR _l "${_i} + 3")
        list(GET _python_externals ${_i} _ext_repo)
        list(GET _python_externals ${_j} _ext_name)
        list(GET _python_externals ${_k} _ext_commit)
        list(GET _python_externals ${_l} _ext_sha256)
        ExternalProject_Add(dep_python3_ext_${_ext_name}
            URL "https://github.com/python/cpython-${_ext_repo}/archive/${_ext_commit}.zip"
            URL_HASH SHA256=${_ext_sha256}
            DOWNLOAD_DIR ${DEP_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/python3
            DOWNLOAD_NAME cpython-${_ext_repo}-${_ext_name}.zip
            SOURCE_DIR "${_python_externals_dir}/${_ext_name}"
            CONFIGURE_COMMAND ""
            BUILD_COMMAND ""
            INSTALL_COMMAND ""
        )
        list(APPEND _python_depends dep_python3_ext_${_ext_name})
    endforeach()
    file(TO_NATIVE_PATH "${_python_externals_dir}" _python_externals_native)

    # PCbuild runs PYTHON without -E, so PYTHONHOME and PYTHONPATH are cleared.
    set(_python_env_args --unset=PYTHONHOME --unset=PYTHONPATH "PYTHON=${_python_host}"
        "EXTERNALS_DIR=${_python_externals_native}"
        "GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=<SOURCE_DIR>/..")

    # CPython's PCbuild needs a 64-bit-hosted toolchain: find_msbuild.bat picks the
    # 32-bit Bin\MSBuild.exe, whose x86 cl.exe/link.exe run out of address space
    # (fatal C1002 "out of heap space") building the LTCG-optimized pythoncore.
    # That 32-bit MSBuild ignores PreferredToolArchitecture, so build.bat must be
    # pointed at a 64-bit MSBuild via the MSBUILD env var. The native arm64 MSBuild
    # then hosts arm64 tools on its own; the amd64 MSBuild still defaults to x86, so
    # PreferredToolArchitecture pins it to x64. Scoped to this build step, so
    # CPython's own sources stay untouched.
    if(CMAKE_GENERATOR_INSTANCE)   # empty for non-VS generators (e.g. Ninja)
        set(_python_msbuild "${CMAKE_GENERATOR_INSTANCE}/MSBuild/Current/Bin/${_python_msbuild_host}/MSBuild.exe")
        if(EXISTS "${_python_msbuild}")
            file(TO_NATIVE_PATH "${_python_msbuild}" _python_msbuild_native)
            list(APPEND _python_env_args "MSBUILD=${_python_msbuild_native}")
        else()
            # Loud signal: a silent fall-through to the 32-bit MSBuild reintroduces C1002.
            message(WARNING "Bundled Python: 64-bit MSBuild not found at '${_python_msbuild}'. "
                "CPython will fall back to find_msbuild.bat's default (32-bit) MSBuild, which may "
                "fail with C1002 (out of heap space) building the optimized pythoncore.")
        endif()
    endif()
    if(_python_tool_arch)
        list(APPEND _python_env_args "PreferredToolArchitecture=${_python_tool_arch}")
    endif()

    # MSBuild reads extra switches from PCbuild/msbuild.rsp.
    set(_python_rsp "/p:PlatformToolset=${_python_platform_toolset}\n")
    # VS 2026's ARM64 code generator needs about 27 GB for one function in
    # Objects/unicodectype.c (python/cpython#153668); the property sheet compiles
    # that file without optimisation.
    if(_python_pcbuild_platform STREQUAL "ARM64")
        file(TO_NATIVE_PATH "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/arm64-unicodectype.props" _python_arm64_props)
        string(APPEND _python_rsp "/p:ForceImportAfterCppTargets=\"${_python_arm64_props}\"\n")
    endif()
    file(WRITE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/python3-msbuild.rsp" "${_python_rsp}")
    set(_conf_cmd
        ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/python3-msbuild.rsp" <SOURCE_DIR>/PCbuild/msbuild.rsp
    )
    set(_build_cmd
        ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E env ${_python_env_args}
        cmd /c PCbuild\\build.bat
            -p ${_python_pcbuild_platform}
            -c ${_python_pcbuild_config}
            --no-tkinter
    )
    set(_install_cmd
        ${CMAKE_COMMAND}
            -DPYTHON_SOURCE_DIR=<SOURCE_DIR>
            -DPYTHON_BUILD_DIR=<SOURCE_DIR>/PCbuild/${_python_pcbuild_output_dir}
            -DPYTHON_DEST_DIR=${DESTDIR}/libpython
            -DPYTHON_LAYOUT_ARCH=${_python_layout_arch}
            -P ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/stage_windows.cmake
    )
elseif(APPLE)
    # macOS configuration
    if(CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES)
        set(_python_target_arch "${CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES}")
    else()
        set(_python_target_arch "${CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR}")
    endif()

    if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "ARM64|arm64|aarch64")
        set(_python_build_arch aarch64)
        set(_python_build_arch_flag "arm64")
    elseif(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "x86_64|AMD64|amd64")
        set(_python_build_arch x86_64)
        set(_python_build_arch_flag "x86_64")
    else()
        set(_python_build_arch "${CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR}")
        set(_python_build_arch_flag "${CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR}")
    endif()

    if(_python_target_arch MATCHES "ARM64|arm64|aarch64")
        set(_python_host_arch aarch64)
        set(_python_arch_flag "arm64")
    elseif(_python_target_arch MATCHES "x86_64|AMD64|amd64")
        set(_python_host_arch x86_64)
        set(_python_arch_flag "x86_64")
    else()
        message(FATAL_ERROR "Unsupported macOS Python target architecture: ${_python_target_arch}")
    endif()

    set(_python_arch_flags "-arch ${_python_arch_flag} -mmacosx-version-min=${CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET}")
    # No -rpath: all other deps are static, so libpython has no shared
    # dependencies to find there. headerpad reserves load-command space for
    # the post-install -add_rpath below.
    set(_python_ldflags "${_python_arch_flags} -Wl,-headerpad_max_install_names")

    # The macOS 27 SDK declares pipe2() and dup3() as available from macOS 27, so
    # configure finds them and CPython 3.12 calls them without a runtime check.
    # Below a macOS 27 deployment target they are weak-linked and resolve to NULL
    # on older systems, where os.pipe() then segfaults -- in `make install`
    # (compileall, ensurepip) and in the shipped app alike. Every configure below
    # keeps the pipe()/dup2() fallbacks (python/cpython#153711).
    if(IS_CROSS_COMPILE)
        set(_python_build_tgt --build=${_python_build_arch}-apple-darwin --host=${_python_host_arch}-apple-darwin)
        set(_python_build_arch_flags "-arch ${_python_build_arch_flag} -mmacosx-version-min=${CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET}")
        set(_python_build_ldflags "${_python_build_arch_flags} -Wl,-rpath,${DESTDIR}/lib")
        set(_python_build_python_dir "<SOURCE_DIR>/build-python-host")
        set(_python_build_python "${_python_build_python_dir}/python")
        set(_conf_cmd
            /bin/sh -c
            "rm -rf '${_python_build_python_dir}' && \
             mkdir -p '${_python_build_python_dir}' && \
             cd '${_python_build_python_dir}' && \
             env \
               CC='${CMAKE_C_COMPILER}' \
               CXX='${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER}' \
               CFLAGS='${_python_build_arch_flags}' \
               CXXFLAGS='${_python_build_arch_flags}' \
               LDFLAGS='${_python_build_ldflags}' \
               MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET='${CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET}' \
               ../configure \
                 --prefix='${_python_build_python_dir}/install' \
                 --enable-shared \
                 --without-static-libpython \
                 --disable-test-modules \
                 --build=${_python_build_arch}-apple-darwin \
                 ac_cv_func_pipe2=no ac_cv_func_dup3=no && \
             make -j${NPROC} python && \
             cd '<SOURCE_DIR>' && \
             env \
               CC='${CMAKE_C_COMPILER}' \
               CXX='${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER}' \
               CFLAGS='${_python_arch_flags}' \
               CXXFLAGS='${_python_arch_flags}' \
               LDFLAGS='${_python_ldflags}' \
               MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET='${CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET}' \
               ./configure \
                 --prefix='${DESTDIR}/libpython' \
                 --enable-shared \
                 --enable-optimizations \
                 --without-static-libpython \
                 --with-openssl='${DESTDIR}' \
                 --disable-test-modules \
                 ac_cv_func_pipe2=no ac_cv_func_dup3=no \
                 ${_python_build_tgt} \
                 --with-build-python='${_python_build_python}' \
                 py_cv_module__tkinter=n/a"
        )
    else()
        set(_python_build_tgt --build=${_python_host_arch}-apple-darwin)
        set(_conf_cmd
            env
            "CC=${CMAKE_C_COMPILER}"
            "CXX=${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER}"

# build host. Normalize once here, before anything links against the dep:
    # give the dylib an @rpath id and teach the interpreter to find it relative
    # to itself. Consumers then just need an rpath entry (src/CMakeLists.txt).
    # install_name_tool invalidates code signatures, so re-sign ad-hoc; CI
    # re-signs the whole bundle with the real identity later.
    # ld collapses '//' in -install_name (but not in -rpath) strings, while
    # ${DESTDIR} ends with a slash -- collapse slashes so -change matches the
    # recorded install name.
    string(REGEX REPLACE "/+" "/" _python_prefix "${DESTDIR}/libpython")
    set(_python_dylib "${_python_prefix}/lib/libpython${_python_version_short}.dylib")
    set(_python_bin "${_python_prefix}/bin/python${_python_version_short}")
    set(_install_cmd make install
        COMMAND install_name_tool -id "@rpath/libpython${_python_version_short}.dylib" "${_python_dylib}"
        COMMAND install_name_tool -change "${_python_dylib}" "@rpath/libpython${_python_version_short}.dylib" "${_python_bin}"
        COMMAND install_name_tool -add_rpath "@loader_path/../lib" "${_python_bin}"
        COMMAND codesign --force --sign - "${_python_dylib}"
        COMMAND codesign --force --sign - "${_python_bin}"
    )
else()
    # Linux/Unix
    # Kept verbatim, no slash normalization (unlike the macOS branch's
    # collapsed copy): the LDFLAGS rpath below is recorded byte-for-byte in
    # the ELF, and the OLD_RPATH handed to relocate_linux.cmake must match it
    # exactly -- both derive from this one variable to make that structural.
    set(_python_prefix "${DESTDIR}/libpython")
    # The rpath points at libpython's real install dir, so the interpreter runs
    # in-tree pre-relocation -- and, critically, it reserves enough RUNPATH
    # bytes for the in-place $ORIGIN rewrite at install time (Flatpak's
    # DESTDIR is the short /app) -- see relocate_linux.cmake.
    set(_conf_cmd ./configure
        --prefix=${_python_prefix}
        --enable-shared
        --enable-optimizations
        --with-openssl=${DESTDIR}
        --without-static-libpython
        --disable-test-modules
        # Tcl/Tk 9.0 is incompatible with CPython 3.12's _tkinter; not needed here.
        py_cv_module__tkinter=n/a
        LDFLAGS=-Wl,-rpath,${_python_prefix}/lib
    )
    set(_build_cmd make -j${NPROC})
    set(_install_cmd make install
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND}
            "-DPYTHON_BIN=${_python_prefix}/bin/python${_python_version_short}"
            "-DOLD_RPATH=${_python_prefix}/lib"
            -P "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/relocate_linux.cmake"
    )
endif()

ExternalProject_Add(dep_python3
    URL "${_python_url}"
    URL_HASH SHA256=${_python_sha256}
    DOWNLOAD_DIR ${DEP_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/python3
    BUILD_IN_SOURCE ON
    CONFIGURE_COMMAND ${_conf_cmd}
    BUILD_COMMAND ${_build_cmd}
    INSTALL_COMMAND ${_install_cmd}
    DEPENDS ${_python_depends}
)

# Python depends on OpenSSL and ZLIB
if(TARGET dep_OpenSSL)
    add_dependencies(dep_python3 dep_OpenSSL)
endif()
if(TARGET dep_ZLIB)
    add_dependencies(dep_python3 dep_ZLIB)
endif()

if (NOT WIN32)
    # _ssl and _hashlib embed the static OpenSSL built in deps/ (Windows uses
    # CPython's prebuilt OpenSSL instead). Their Makefile rules depend only on
    # their own sources, not on the OpenSSL archives, so a rebuilt OpenSSL does
    # not make them relink and they keep the previous one. On an incremental tree,
    # drop the built modules and relink them against the current OpenSSL; a
    # fresh build is left alone (its PGO target builds them). "make" alone is a
    # no-op once PGO has run, so sharedmods is invoked explicitly.
    ExternalProject_Get_Property(dep_python3 SOURCE_DIR)
    file(GLOB _python_ssl_modules
        "${SOURCE_DIR}/Modules/_ssl*.so"
        "${SOURCE_DIR}/Modules/_hashlib*.so")
    if (_python_ssl_modules)
        ExternalProject_Add_Step(dep_python3 relink_ssl_extensions
            DEPENDEES configure
            DEPENDERS build
            COMMAND sh -c "rm -f '${SOURCE_DIR}'/Modules/_ssl*.so '${SOURCE_DIR}'/Modules/_hashlib*.so && make -j${NPROC} sharedmods"
            WORKING_DIRECTORY "${SOURCE_DIR}"
            COMMENT "CPython: relinking _ssl/_hashlib against the current OpenSSL"
            DEPENDS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_FILE}"
                    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/../OpenSSL/OpenSSL.cmake"
        )
    endif ()
endif ()

on:

    inputs:
      cache-key:
        required: true

        required: true

jobs:
  build_deps:
    name: Build Deps
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && (inputs.build-deps-only || inputs.force-build || inputs.valid-cache != true) }}
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.os }}
    env:
      date:
    steps:

      # Setup the environment
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          lfs: 'false'

      - name: load cached deps
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ inputs.cache-path }}
          key: ${{ inputs.cache-key }}

      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"  # use most recent 4.3.x version
          useLocalCache: true         # <--= Use the local cache (default is 'false').
          useCloudCache: true

      - name: setup dev on Windows
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        uses: microsoft/setup-msbuild@v3

      - name: Get the date on Ubuntu and macOS
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        run: echo "date=$(date +'%Y%m%d')" >> $GITHUB_ENV
        shell: bash

      - name: Get the date on Windows
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: echo "date=$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd')" | Out-File -Append -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8
        shell: pwsh


      - name: Install MSYS2 (clangarm64) with GMP/MPFR and LLVM tools
        if: runner.os == 'Windows' && inputs.arch == 'arm64'
        uses: msys2/setup-msys2@v2
        with:
          msystem: CLANGARM64
          update: true
          install: >-
            mingw-w64-clang-aarch64-gmp
            mingw-w64-clang-aarch64-mpfr
            mingw-w64-clang-aarch64-llvm

      - name: Stage ARM64 GMP/MPFR (no prebuilt blobs exist for win-arm64)
        # GMP/MPFR ship prebuilt x64/x86 blobs in-tree but none for ARM64.
        # Pull them from MSYS2 clangarm64 and generate MSVC import libs via
        # llvm-dlltool, then stage into deps/{GMP,MPFR}/.../win-arm64 where the
        # MSVC branch of GMP.cmake/MPFR.cmake copies them into the dep prefix.
        if: runner.os == 'Windows' && inputs.arch == 'arm64'
        shell: msys2 {0}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          BIN=/clangarm64/bin
          REPO=$(cygpath -u "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE")

          make_import_lib() {
            local dll="$1"; local lib="$2"; local def="/tmp/${dll%.dll}.def"
            echo "EXPORTS" > "$def"
            llvm-readobj --coff-exports "$BIN/$dll" | awk '/Name: /{print $2}' >> "$def"
            llvm-dlltool -m arm64 -D "$dll" -d "$def" -l "$BIN/$lib"
          }

          make_import_lib libgmp-10.dll libgmp-10.lib

          # MPFR 4.x ships as libmpfr-6.dll; rename to libmpfr-4 BEFORE generating
          # the import lib so the baked-in runtime DLL name is correct.
          MPFR_DLL=$(ls $BIN/libmpfr-*.dll | head -1 | xargs basename)
          if [ "$MPFR_DLL" != "libmpfr-4.dll" ]; then cp "$BIN/$MPFR_DLL" "$BIN/libmpfr-4.dll"; fi
          make_import_lib libmpfr-4.dll libmpfr-4.lib

          mkdir -p $REPO/deps/GMP/gmp/lib/win-arm64 $REPO/deps/MPFR/mpfr/lib/win-arm64
          cp $BIN/libgmp-10.dll $BIN/libgmp-10.lib $REPO/deps/GMP/gmp/lib/win-arm64/
          cp $BIN/libmpfr-4.dll $BIN/libmpfr-4.lib $REPO/deps/MPFR/mpfr/lib/win-arm64/
          cp /clangarm64/include/gmp.h  $REPO/deps/GMP/gmp/include/
          cp /clangarm64/include/mpfr.h $REPO/deps/MPFR/mpfr/include/ || true

      # Build Dependencies
      - name: Build on Windows
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
            if (-not "${{ vars.SELF_HOSTED }}") {
              choco install strawberryperl
            }
            # cache-path is the install directory inside the deps build directory.
            $deps = (Split-Path "${{ github.workspace }}/${{ inputs.cache-path }}").Replace('\', '/')
            # -l compiles with Visual Studio's clang-cl and -x builds with Ninja; --msvc --msbuild is cl under the Visual Studio generator.
            $flags = if ("${{ inputs.compiler }}" -eq "clang") { "-l", "-x" } else { "--msvc", "--msbuild" }
            .\build_win.bat -d --arch ${{ inputs.arch }} --deps-dir $deps @flags
        shell: pwsh

      - name: Build on Mac ${{ inputs.arch }}
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
            if [ -z "${{ vars.SELF_HOSTED }}" ]; then
              brew install automake texinfo libtool pkgconf yasm nasm
            fi
            ./build_release_macos.sh -dx ${{ !vars.SELF_HOSTED && '-j 3' || '' }} -a ${{ inputs.arch }} -t 10.15
            (cd "${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build/${{ inputs.arch }}" && \
            find . -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name 'OrcaSlicer_dep' -exec rm -rf {} +)


      - name: Apt-Install Dependencies
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && !vars.SELF_HOSTED
        uses: ./.github/actions/apt-install-deps

      - name: Build on Ubuntu
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
            mkdir -p ${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build/destdir
            ./build_linux.sh -drlL
            cd deps/build
            tar -czvf OrcaSlicer_dep_ubuntu_$(date +"%Y%m%d").tar.gz destdir


      # Upload Artifacts
      # - name: Upload Mac ${{ inputs.arch }} artifacts
      #   if: runner.os == 'macOS'
      #   uses: actions/upload-artifact@v6
      #   with:
      #     name: OrcaSlicer_dep_mac_${{ env.date }}
      #     path: ${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep*.tar.gz

      # - name: Upload Windows artifacts

      #   with:
      #     name: OrcaSlicer_dep_win64_${{ env.date }}
      #     path: ${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep*.zip

      # - name: Upload Ubuntu artifacts
      #   if: runner.os == 'Linux' && !env.ACT
      #   env:
      #     ubuntu-ver: '2404'
      #   uses: actions/upload-artifact@v6
      #   with:

      #     path: ${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep_ubuntu_*.tar.gz

  build_orca:
    name: Build OrcaSlicer
    needs: [build_deps]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && !inputs.build-deps-only && (inputs.force-build || (inputs.valid-cache == true && needs.build_deps.result == 'skipped') || (inputs.valid-cache != true && success())) }}

name: JusPrin build all

# Every platform of JusPrin from one commit, for jusprin_release.yml (a draft
# release) and jusprin_nightly.yml (the nightly-builds pre-release).
#
# Each platform is built by jusprin_release_build.yml; the macos job joins the
# two macOS architectures into the universal app and its disk image. The
# files are left as this run's artifacts named jusprin-*, for the caller to
# collect: the Windows x64 installer and portable zip, the macOS universal
# disk image, the Linux x64 AppImage, and the per-architecture Mac bundles,
# which only feed the universal app.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      version:
        required: true
        type: string
      # Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets JusPrin 1.x
      # used. Windows builds are unsigned.
      sign_macos:
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.name }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: Windows x64
            os: windows-latest
            arch: x64
          - name: macOS arm64
            os: macos-15
            arch: arm64
          - name: macOS x86_64
            os: macos-15
            arch: x86_64
          - name: Linux x64
            os: ubuntu-24.04
            arch: ''
    uses: ./.github/workflows/jusprin_release_build.yml
    with:
      os: ${{ matrix.os }}
      arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
      version: ${{ inputs.version }}
    secrets: inherit

  macos:
    name: macOS universal
    needs: build
    # A self-hosted Mac when JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER is set, as in jusprin_release_build.yml.
    runs-on: ${{ vars.JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER && fromJSON(format('["self-hosted","{0}"]', vars.JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER)) || 'macos-15' }}
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      SIGN: ${{ inputs.sign_macos && '1' || '0' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'

      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"
          useLocalCache: true
          useCloudCache: true

      - name: Get both architectures
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: jusprin-macOS-*
          path: mac_bundles
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Join them into the universal app
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/arm64 build/x86_64
          tar -xzf mac_bundles/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_arm64.tar.gz -C build/arm64
          tar -xzf mac_bundles/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_x86_64.tar.gz -C build/x86_64
          ./build_release_macos.sh -u -x -j 1 -a universal -t 10.15

      # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml loads the certificate, with the secret
      # names JusPrin 1.x used.
      - name: Load the signing certificate
        if: env.SIGN == '1'
        env:
          BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 }}
          P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.P12_PASSWORD }}
          KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          certificate="$RUNNER_TEMP/build_certificate.p12"
          keychain="$RUNNER_TEMP/app-signing.keychain-db"
          # What the steps below replace, for the last step to put back: on a
          # self-hosted Mac these are its owner's own keychain settings.
          security default-keychain -d user | xargs > "$RUNNER_TEMP/default-keychain"
          security list-keychains -d user | xargs > "$RUNNER_TEMP/keychain-list"
          echo -n "$BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64" | base64 --decode --output "$certificate"
          security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$keychain"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$keychain"
          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$keychain"
          security default-keychain -s "$keychain"
          security import "$certificate" -P "$P12_PASSWORD" -A -t cert -f pkcs12 -k "$keychain"
          security list-keychain -d user -s "$keychain"
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s -k "$P12_PASSWORD" "$keychain"

      - name: Make the disk image
        env:
          JUSPRIN_SIGN: ${{ env.SIGN }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT: ${{ secrets.APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT }}
          TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.TEAM_ID }}
          APP_PWD: ${{ secrets.APP_PWD }}
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/macos_package.sh \
            build/universal/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app "$VERSION" dist

      # Puts back the user's default keychain and keychain list, and deletes
      # the signing keychain, even when an earlier step failed.
      - name: Restore the keychains
        if: always() && env.SIGN == '1'
        run: |
          [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/keychain-list" ] || exit 0
          read -r -a keychains < "$RUNNER_TEMP/keychain-list"
          security list-keychains -d user -s "${keychains[@]}"
          security default-keychain -d user -s "$(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/default-keychain")"
          keychain="$RUNNER_TEMP/app-signing.keychain-db"
          [ ! -e "$keychain" ] || security delete-keychain "$keychain"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jusprin-macOS-universal
          path: dist/*.dmg
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

content.text: Reading the release workflow that builds each Mac architecture, to see where the deps (including Python) come from.

input.command: cat .github/workflows/jusprin_release_build.yml
input.description: Read the per-platform release build workflow

result.output:
name: JusPrin release build

# One platform of a JusPrin release, called by jusprin_release.yml.
#
# The build is OrcaSlicer's: its dependency workflow (build_deps.yml), cached
# under the key OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml uses, and its build
# scripts. Only the packaging is JusPrin's (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging).
# OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml can't be reused as it is: its Linux step looks
# for OrcaSlicer_Linux_V<version>.AppImage, which a JusPrin build never
# writes, and its packaging steps name everything OrcaSlicer.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      os:
        required: true
        type: string
      # x64 (Windows), arm64 or x86_64 (macOS); empty for Linux amd64, as in
      # OrcaSlicer's build_all.yml.
      arch:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      version:
        required: true
        type: string

jobs:
  cache:
    name: Find the deps cache
    # GitHub often has no hosted macOS runner free, and cancels a job that gets
    # none within 15 minutes, so the macOS lookup runs on Linux, as in
    # OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml.
    runs-on: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && 'ubuntu-24.04' || inputs.os }}
    outputs:
      key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
      path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
      hit: ${{ steps.lookup.outputs.cache-hit }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'
      - name: Compute the key
        id: key
        shell: bash
        env:
          # As in OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml. The macOS and Linux trees are
          # OrcaSlicer's and share its cache; OrcaSlicer builds Windows with clang-cl,
          # so JusPrin's cl tree is cached on its own.
          cache_os: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && format('{0}-{1}', inputs.os, inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && format('windows-{0}-msvc', inputs.arch) || format('linux-clang{0}', inputs.arch && format('-{0}', inputs.arch) || '')) }}
          OS: ${{ inputs.os }}
          dep_folder: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && format('/{0}', inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && inputs.arch == 'arm64') && '-arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep' || '/OrcaSlicer_dep' }}
        run: |
          echo "key=${cache_os}-cache-orcaslicer_deps-build-${{ hashFiles('deps/**') }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Relative to the workspace, as build_deps.yml takes it.
          echo "path=deps/build${dep_folder}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # The workspace of a hosted macOS job, where build_deps.yml saved the tree.
          if [[ "$OS" == macos-* ]]; then
            echo "macos_workspace=/Users/runner/work/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      # actions/cache matches the path too, so a Linux lookup for macOS names the
      # macOS workspace.
      - name: Look the cache up
        id: lookup
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.macos_workspace || github.workspace }}/${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
          key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
          lookup-only: true

  deps:
    name: Build deps
    needs: cache
    if: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.hit != 'true' }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/build_deps.yml
    with:
      cache-key: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.key }}
      cache-path: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}
      valid-cache: false
      os: ${{ inputs.os }}
      arch: ${{ inputs.arch }}
      # cl under the Visual Studio generator, which JusPrin's Windows build uses.
      compiler: msvc
      # Stops build_deps.yml before it calls OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml.
      build-deps-only: true
    secrets: inherit

  build:
    name: Build JusPrin
    needs: [cache, deps]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.cache.result == 'success' && (needs.deps.result == 'success' || needs.deps.result == 'skipped') }}
    # The repository variable JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER, when set, sends the Mac
    # builds to a self-hosted runner with that label instead of GitHub's
    # macos-15, whose queue can cancel a job that waits too long for a
    # machine. inputs.os stays macos-15, so the deps cache keeps its key.
    runs-on: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && vars.JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER && fromJSON(format('["self-hosted","{0}"]', vars.JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER)) || inputs.os }}
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      # The Sentry project the app's error reports go to, read by
      # JusPrin/sources.cmake; kept out of the public repository.
      JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN: ${{ secrets.JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN }}
      # The pages' build, which their error reports carry and their source
      # maps are filed under in Sentry (WebShared/errorReports.ts).
      JUSPRIN_PAGE_BUILD: ${{ github.sha }}
    steps:
      # A build without it sends no error report or crash, which nobody would
      # notice until reports were needed.
      - name: Require the Sentry key
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ -z "$JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN" ]; then
            echo "::error::The secret JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN is missing, so this build would send no error report or crash."
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'

      - name: Load the deps
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}
          key: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.key }}
          fail-on-cache-miss: true

      # The same CMake as OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml.
      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"
          useLocalCache: true
          useCloudCache: true

      # The Agent and Home pages are built with npm (JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt).
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      # Windows
      - name: Set up MSVC
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        uses: microsoft/setup-msbuild@v3

      - name: Install NSIS
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: choco install nsis

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml calls build_win.bat, but with cl rather than
        # clang-cl. -i installs into build\OrcaSlicer, which the packaging reads.
        run: |
          $deps = (Split-Path "${{ github.workspace }}/${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}").Replace('\', '/')
          .\build_win.bat -s -i --arch ${{ inputs.arch }} --build-dir build --deps-dir $deps --msvc --msbuild

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/windows_package.ps1 -BuildDir build -Version $env:VERSION `
            -Arch "${{ inputs.arch }}" -OutDir dist

      # macOS: each architecture is built here; jusprin_release.yml joins them
      # into the universal app and the disk image.
      - name: Prepare the Mac
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install libtool
          mkdir -p "${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build/${{ inputs.arch }}"
          # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml does, for disk space: keep only the
          # selected Xcode. Only on GitHub's machines: a self-hosted Mac is
          # someone's own computer.
          if [ "$RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT" = github-hosted ]; then
            xcode=$(basename "$(cd "$(xcode-select -p)/../.." && pwd -P)")
            sudo find /Applications -maxdepth 1 -type d -name "Xcode_*.app" ! -name "$xcode" -exec rm -rf {} +
            sudo rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Caches/*
          fi

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        # Line tables (-gline-tables-only) let Sentry give the file and line
        # of each frame; they go into the dSYM below, not into the app.
        run: >-
          ./build_release_macos.sh -s -n -x -j 3 -a ${{ inputs.arch }} -t 10.15 --
          -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-gline-tables-only -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-gline-tables-only

      # The line tables stay in the build's object files; dsymutil gathers
      # them into a dSYM for Sentry, and strip -S then drops the executable's
      # pointers to those files. The executable keeps its function names.
      - name: Split the debug information
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          bin="build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer"
          dsymutil "$bin" -o "build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer.dSYM"
          strip -S "$bin"

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          tar -czf "dist/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_${{ inputs.arch }}.tar.gz" -C "build/${{ inputs.arch }}" OrcaSlicer

      # Linux
      - name: Install the build packages
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        uses: ./.github/actions/apt-install-deps

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          # -s builds the slicer and lays out build/package; JusPrin's AppImage
          # replaces OrcaSlicer's (-i). Line tables (-gline-tables-only) let
          # Sentry give the file and line of each frame; they are split off
          # below, not shipped.
          ./build_linux.sh -srlL -- -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-gline-tables-only -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-gline-tables-only
          ./scripts/check_appimage_libs.sh ./build/package ./build/package/bin/orca-slicer

      # Sentry files a debug file by the executable's GNU build id, which the
      # split file keeps; without one the two would not match.
      - name: Split the debug information
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          bin=build/package/bin/orca-slicer
          readelf -n "$bin" | grep -q 'Build ID' || {
            echo "::error::$bin has no GNU build id, so Sentry could not match its debug file to it."
            exit 1
          }
          objcopy --only-keep-debug "$bin" build/orca-slicer.debug
          objcopy --strip-debug --add-gnu-debuglink=build/orca-slicer.debug "$bin"

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/appimage.sh build/package "$VERSION" \
            "dist/JusPrin_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_V${VERSION}${{ inputs.arch && format('_{0}', inputs.arch) || '' }}.AppImage"

      # OrcaSlicer.pdb is over 2 GiB, and JusPrin's Sentry (self-hosted 23.1.1)
      # stores no file larger than that: its file table keeps offsets in a
      # 32-bit integer. Mozilla's dump_syms turns the PDB into a Breakpad
      # symbol file, about a quarter of its size, with the same build id and
      # each function's file and line; Sentry shows no inlined frames from it.
      - name: Convert the app's PDB to Breakpad for Sentry
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $zip = "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\dump_syms.zip"
          Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -OutFile $zip `
            https://github.com/mozilla/dump_syms/releases/download/v2.3.9/dump_syms-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip
          if ((Get-FileHash $zip -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne 'BDF48486220708808A3E00AEC78856EE1CCE096189D47A1E2CB1C635F93BACC7') {
            throw "dump_syms-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip does not have the checksum of dump_syms 2.3.9."
          }
          Expand-Archive $zip "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\dump_syms"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force build\sentry-breakpad | Out-Null
          & "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\dump_syms\dump_syms.exe" build\src\Release\OrcaSlicer.pdb -o build\sentry-breakpad\OrcaSlicer.sym
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }

      # What lets Sentry name the functions in a crash or a report's stack: each
      # executable and library the app ships, filed by its build id, and the
      # debug information split off above (on Windows, the Breakpad file made
      # from OrcaSlicer.pdb and the launcher's own small PDB). The build fails
      # unless Sentry then holds the app's own code's debug information, with
      # file and line (Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh). Sentry's address and
      # the token that may upload stay in the repository's secrets.
      - name: Upload debug files to Sentry
        shell: bash
        env:
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          SENTRY_URL: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_URL }}
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
        run: |
          case "$RUNNER_OS" in
            Windows) main=build/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.dll; paths=(build/OrcaSlicer build/src/Release/orca-slicer.pdb build/sentry-breakpad) ;;
            macOS)
              app="build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app"
              main="$app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer"; paths=("$app/Contents" "build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer.dSYM") ;;
            *) main=build/package/bin/orca-slicer; paths=(build/package/bin build/package/lib build/orca-slicer.debug) ;;
          esac
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh upload "$main" "${paths[@]}"

      # What lets Sentry name the Agent and Home pages' code in a page error's
      # stack: each page and its source map, filed under this commit. Every
      # platform builds the same pages; the step fails if one differs.
      - name: Upload page source maps to Sentry
        shell: bash
        env:
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          SENTRY_URL: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_URL }}
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
        run: ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh upload

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jusprin-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.arch || 'x64' }}
          path: dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error
          # The release keeps the files; these only carry them to it.
          retention-days: 7

=== 9196e41439 Release build: keep the self-hosted Mac's own libraries out of the app
A test build on Kenneth's Mac linked the app's OpenGL from XQuartz
(/opt/X11) and Python's _blake2 and _lzma modules from Homebrew, and
the x86_64 Python build failed on Homebrew's arm64 libb2. The app would
not start on a Mac without XQuartz.

Two routes let those libraries in. Homebrew's pkg-config hands its
libraries to the autotools deps (Python, FFmpeg), so on the self-hosted
Mac pkg-config now looks only in the deps' own folder. And
build_release_macos.sh joins its CMake ignore list with colons, which
CMake reads as one folder that does not exist, so the app build there
gets a semicolon list that also names XQuartz's folders.

mac_outside_links.sh lists every program and library that loads a
library from outside macOS and itself. Kept deps that fail it are built
again, and newly built deps or an app that fail it stop the build. It
runs only on the self-hosted Mac: the 2.0.0 app built on GitHub's Macs
already has one such link (_lzma loads Homebrew's xz), and its cached
deps would fail the check until they are rebuilt.

=== cabdc437fd Release build: keep XQuartz's OpenGL out of the self-hosted Mac's deps
The test build on the jusprin-ci account still linked the app's OpenGL
from /opt/X11. The wxWidgets dep had found /usr/X11R6/lib/libGL.dylib
while the deps were built and wrote it into wxWidgetsTargets.cmake and
its wx-config file, and the app takes OpenGL from there. The semicolon
ignore list only reached the app's own CMake: deps/CMakeLists.txt hands
build_release_macos.sh's colon-joined list on to every dep, where it
ignores nothing.

mac_self_hosted.cmake is a toolchain file that adds Homebrew, MacPorts
and XQuartz to CMAKE_SYSTEM_IGNORE_PREFIX_PATH. deps/CMakeLists.txt
passes CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE on to every dep, so on the self-hosted Mac
the deps and the app builds get it from the environment. Tried locally
with XQuartz installed: without it CMake takes /usr/X11R6/lib/libGL.dylib
and Homebrew's libb2; with it, from the environment or passed on as the
deps do, it takes the OpenGL framework and finds no libb2.

mac_outside_links.sh now also reads the deps' CMake, pkg-config, libtool
and wx-config files for a library file in those folders, or one after
-L, since a static library's own load commands are empty. It flags the
kept arm64 and x86_64 deps' wxWidgets files and nothing else, so the
next run builds both again.

# Making a JusPrin release

The release workflow, `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml`, builds the
release files from one commit and uploads them to a draft release on GitHub.
It refuses the commit without a new version, release notes, a guide check and
the Sentry secrets, and fails a platform whose debug files or page source
maps did not reach Sentry (see "Releasing" in `AGENTS.md`). It does not run the test suites, check the
server, check the translations or audit error handling. This skill covers
those too, in the order they have to happen.

## Kenneth decides these

Ask Kenneth, in plain words, and wait for his yes before each of these. A yes
covers that one action, not the next one.

- The version number, when he has not named it.
- The release notes' wording. Show him the file.
- Deploying the server.
- Which error-handling findings must be fixed before the release.
- Taking in commits that landed on `jusprin-dev` after the range was fixed.
- The Sentry values and read-only token for checking the draft.
- Spending API money on live AI checks. Say the cost.
- Pushing to `jusprin-dev`, and moving `main` forward.
- Starting the release workflow.
- Downloading the draft's files to this computer.
- Posting anything on GitHub, such as replies to issues.

**Never publish the draft.** Kenneth publishes it by hand on the Releases page.
Never force-push `main`.

## When something has to be fixed

A fix for anything a step finds is its own commit on `jusprin-dev`, never
part of the release commit. Make it in a worktree of its own, on a branch
from `origin/jusprin-dev`, not in your release worktree. Pushing it needs
Kenneth's yes. Once it is on `origin/jusprin-dev`:

- **Before section 8 landed the release commit:** commit your release edits
  on your branch, rebase onto `origin/jusprin-dev`, and write down that
  commit as the new end of the range. Then redo step 1.4 and sections 2 to 7
  for the whole range. A fix can need a line in the notes, a translation, or
  a change to a test or the guide.
- **After it landed (a problem found in section 9 or 10):** the version is
  not released yet, so keep it. The new end of the range is the fix's commit
  on `origin/jusprin-dev`. Redo step 1.4 and sections 2 to 7 on a branch
  from it, land what changed as in section 8, move `main` to the new release
  commit, and start the workflow again (section 9). A new run for the same
  version replaces the draft's files and text.

If a step fails and you cannot tell why, stop and tell Kenneth with the
output. Do not skip the step.

## Where each platform is tested

Every release is tested on all three platforms, twice: the test suites in
section 5, and the draft's own files in section 10. A platform that was not
tested blocks the release; it is not a line in the report.

ASSISTANT : Yes, it can be done on GitHub's Macs. I haven't tried it yet; here is what the code shows.

**Why the build picks up Homebrew's library.** Python's build script looks for optional libraries on the machine it runs on. GitHub's Mac images come with Homebrew and its `xz` package already installed. So the build finds Homebrew's `liblzma` and links the `_lzma` module (Python's compression module) against `/opt/homebrew/...`. A Mac without Homebrew has nothing at that path.

The recipe, `deps/python3/python3.cmake`, already handles the same kind of problem for one module. Around line 291 it switches off `_tkinter` with `py_cv_module__tkinter=n/a`, because Homebrew's Tcl/Tk breaks it. The recipe appears to come from upstream OrcaSlicer: its commits carry OrcaSlicer pull-request numbers, but I haven't checked them with `git blame`.

**Two ways to fix it on GitHub's Macs:**

1. **Leave the module out.** Add `py_cv_module__lzma=n/a` next to the tkinter line. That's one line, and `_lzma` is then never built, so nothing links to Homebrew. The cost: `import lzma` fails on every Mac, including Macs where it works today. I haven't checked whether anything in JusPrin or its plug-ins uses `lzma`. My guess is nothing does, but I'd search before choosing this.
2. **Build `xz` ourselves.** Add `xz` as a dependency and point Python at our copy, the way it already gets our OpenSSL. `lzma` then works everywhere, but this is a bigger change to a file owned by upstream OrcaSlicer, and every future upstream merge has to carry it.

**Either way, the first build is slow.** Changing the dependency recipe changes the cache key, so the next GitHub build rebuilds all dependencies for both chips. That takes about an hour more, once.

Two more things:
- The outside-library check (`mac_outside_links.sh`) is so far only on my unlanded branch for your Mac. Landing it in the GitHub build would fail any future build that links Homebrew again, instead of us finding out after a release.
- The check found only `_lzma` in 2.0.1, so this one line or one dependency should be the whole fix.

If you want it, I'd do the first way after a search shows nothing uses `lzma`, and land it with the check, as a fix for the next release. I don't think it needs to hold up 2.0.1, because 2.0.0 shipped with the same link.

+++ b/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/mac_outside_links.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Usage: mac_outside_links.sh <folder> [<allowed folder>...]
+#
+# Lists every program and library under <folder> that loads a library from
+# outside macOS (/usr/lib, /System), outside itself (@rpath, @loader_path,
+# @executable_path) and outside the allowed folders, and exits 1 if there is
+# one. A Mac that builds JusPrin can have Homebrew or XQuartz installed, and a
+# build that links their libraries runs there but fails on a Mac without them.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+dir=$1
+shift
+allowed=("$@")
+
+found=0
+while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
+  # Only the load commands: a library's own install name is not a load.
+  while IFS= read -r lib; do
+    case "$lib" in
+      /usr/lib/* | /System/* | @rpath/* | @loader_path/* | @executable_path/*) continue ;;
+    esac
+    ok=0
+    for prefix in "${allowed[@]+"${allowed[@]}"}"; do
+      case "$lib" in "$prefix"/*) ok=1 ;; esac
+    done
+    if [ "$ok" = 0 ]; then
+      echo "$file loads $lib"
+      found=1
+    fi
+  done < <(otool -l "$file" 2>/dev/null |
+    awk '/cmd LC_(LOAD|LOAD_WEAK|REEXPORT|LAZY_LOAD|LOAD_UPWARD)_DYLIB$/ { load = 1; next }
+         load && $1 == "name" { print $2; load = 0 }' | sort -u)
+done < <(find "$dir" -type f \( -name '*.dylib' -o -name '*.so' -o -perm -u+x \) -print0)
+
+# A static library loads nothing itself, but its CMake, pkg-config, libtool
+# or wx-config files hand the libraries it needs to whatever links it: a
+# library file's absolute path, or a folder after -L. Those must not be in
+# Homebrew, MacPorts or XQuartz. (A folder a Find module merely searches is
+# neither.)
+outside='(-L|^|[[:space:]"'"'"';=(])(/opt/homebrew|/usr/local|/opt/local|/opt/X11|/usr/X11R6|/usr/X11)/[^[:space:]"'"'"';)]*'
+while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
+  links=$(grep -E -o "$outside" "$file" |
+    sed -E 's/^[[:space:]"'"'"';=(]//' |
+    grep -E '^-L|\.(dylib|tbd|so|a|la)$|\.framework' | sort -u || true)
+  if [ -n "$links" ]; then
+    echo "$links" | sed "s|^|$file links |"
+    found=1
+  fi
+done < <(find "$dir" -type f \( -name '*.cmake' -o -name '*.pc' -o -name '*.la' -o -path '*/wx/config/*' \) -print0)
+
+exit "$found"

#!/bin/bash
# Sets up the macOS user that builds JusPrin's Mac release jobs, so that the
# builds never see the libraries in /opt/homebrew, /usr/local or XQuartz.
#
# Run it from Kenneth's own account, in Terminal:
#
#   sudo RUNNER_TOKEN="$(gh api -X POST repos/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/actions/runners/registration-token -q .token)" \
#     bash "<this file>"
#
# It asks for Kenneth's password (sudo), then for a password for the new
# account (sysadminctl). Nobody needs to log in as that account afterwards.
# Running it again skips what is already done.
#
# What it does:
# 1. Creates the standard (non-admin) user jusprin-ci, hidden from the login
#    window.
# 2. Clones Homebrew into /Users/jusprin-ci/homebrew and installs only the seven
#    tools the build needs. Kenneth's /opt/homebrew is not touched.
# 3. Downloads the GitHub Actions runner into /Users/jusprin-ci/actions-runner,
#    checks its published SHA-256, and registers it with the label
#    jusprin-release-mac. Its PATH is that Homebrew plus macOS's own folders.
# 4. Runs it as a LaunchDaemon with UserName jusprin-ci, so it starts at boot
#    without anyone logging in as that user.
set -euo pipefail

ci_user=jusprin-ci
home=/Users/$ci_user
repo=TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin
label=jusprin-release-mac
name=kenneth-mac-jusprin-ci
runner_version=2.338.2
runner_sha=25a065af409ffa317ab4d5a3b614dd15fc9c40f2172bc1b35a1b1258e919a388
tools="automake libtool texinfo pkgconf yasm nasm gettext"
path="$home/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin"
plist=/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.jusprin.ci-runner.plist

if [ "$(id -u)" != 0 ]; then
  echo "Run this with sudo (see the top of the file)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ -z "${RUNNER_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  echo "RUNNER_TOKEN is empty: run it as the top of the file shows." >&2
  exit 1
fi

as_ci() {
  sudo -u "$ci_user" env -i HOME="$home" USER="$ci_user" LOGNAME="$ci_user" LANG=en_US.UTF-8 \
    PATH="$path" HOMEBREW_NO_ANALYTICS=1 HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_ENV_HINTS=1 "$@"
}

echo "== 1. The account"
if ! id "$ci_user" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Type a password for the new account $ci_user:"
  sysadminctl -addUser "$ci_user" -fullName "JusPrin CI" -shell /bin/zsh -home "$home" -password -
  dscl . create "/Users/$ci_user" IsHidden 1
fi
createhomedir -c -u "$ci_user" > /dev/null
id "$ci_user"

echo "== 2. Its own Homebrew and the build tools"
if [ ! -x "$home/homebrew/bin/brew" ]; then
  as_ci git clone -q --depth 1 https://github.com/Homebrew/brew "$home/homebrew"
fi
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
as_ci "$home/homebrew/bin/brew" install $tools

echo "== 3. The runner"
runner=$home/actions-runner
as_ci mkdir -p "$runner" "$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner"
if [ ! -x "$runner/config.sh" ]; then
  tarball=$runner/runner.tar.gz
  as_ci curl -fsSL -o "$tarball" \
    "https://github.com/actions/runner/releases/download/v$runner_version/actions-runner-osx-arm64-$runner_version.tar.gz"
  echo "$runner_sha  $tarball" | shasum -a 256 -c -
  as_ci tar -xzf "$tarball" -C "$runner"
  rm -f "$tarball"
fi
if [ ! -f "$runner/.runner" ]; then
  as_ci bash -c "cd '$runner' && ./config.sh --unattended --url 'https://github.com/$repo' \
    --token '$RUNNER_TOKEN' --name '$name' --labels '$label' --work _work"
fi
# Jobs get this PATH: never /opt/homebrew, /usr/local or /opt/X11.
echo "$path" | as_ci tee "$runner/.path" > /dev/null
# The service starts runsvc.sh from the runner's folder, as the runner's own
# svc.sh install puts it there.
as_ci cp "$runner/bin/runsvc.sh" "$runner/runsvc.sh"
as_ci chmod u+x "$runner/runsvc.sh"

echo "== 4. The service"
new_plist=$(mktemp)
cat > "$new_plist" <<EOF
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
  <dict>
    <key>Label</key>
    <string>com.jusprin.ci-runner</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
      <string>$runner/runsvc.sh</string>
    </array>
    <key>UserName</key>
    <string>$ci_user</string>
    <key>WorkingDirectory</key>
    <string>$runner</string>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    <true/>
    <key>KeepAlive</key>
    <dict>
      <key>SuccessfulExit</key>
      <false/>
    </dict>
    <key>StandardOutPath</key>
    <string>$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner/stdout.log</string>
    <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
    <string>$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner/stderr.log</string>
    <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
    <dict>
      <key>ACTIONS_RUNNER_SVC</key>
      <string>1</string>
      <key>HOME</key>
      <string>$home</string>
      <key>USER</key>
      <string>$ci_user</string>
      <key>LANG</key>
      <string>en_US.UTF-8</string>
      <key>PATH</key>
      <string>$path</string>
    </dict>
    <key>ProcessType</key>
    <string>Interactive</string>
    <key>SessionCreate</key>
    <true/>
  </dict>
</plist>
EOF
# Restarting the service ends the job it is running, so it is restarted only
# when the service file changed or the service is not loaded.
if cmp -s "$new_plist" "$plist" && launchctl print system/com.jusprin.ci-runner > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  rm -f "$new_plist"
  echo "The service is unchanged and loaded; left running."
else
  mv "$new_plist" "$plist"
  chown root:wheel "$plist"
  chmod 644 "$plist"
  launchctl bootout system "$plist" 2> /dev/null || true
  launchctl bootstrap system "$plist"
  sleep 5
fi
launchctl print system/com.jusprin.ci-runner | grep -E "state|pid" | head -3
echo "Done. The runner $name should show as Idle on GitHub within a minute."

The search turned up no single definitive fix for this exact combination, but several threads point to the same likely causes.

- **Missing intermediate certificate:** An Apple Developer Forums reply says the "self-signed root" wording suggests that you're missing an intermediate certificate. Reinstalling the Apple intermediates and roots from Apple's certificate authority page did not fix it for one user, so check the chain itself, not only the signing identity. Tried explicit --keychain argument in codesign (no change) in that same thread.
- **Keychain context matters:** A thread about a LaunchDaemon says that after finds a valid identity to sign with now, the fix also had to add the Apple Worldwide Developer Relation cert to the system keychain. Another thread describes a CI setup where the signing certificate lived in a non-root user's login keychain, which was the user running GitHub Actions jobs (certificates being present on the non root user's login keychain, which was also the user executing jobs for github actions in our case).
- **Session type:** Other reports show the same error appearing only over SSH. One Apple thread is titled codesign fails when started from SSH, succeed in Terminal, and a Lightrun answer describes hitting the error over an ssh session.

For your self-hosted runner, the most likely problem is that the LaunchDaemon runs outside the logged-in user's session, so it can't reach the signing identity or its private key in the login keychain. Possible fixes are to run the runner as a LaunchAgent in the logged-in session, put the signing identity in a keychain the daemon can unlock, and make sure the full Apple intermediate chain (including the WWDR cert) is installed. I didn't find a source that confirms this exact setup, so verify it on your machine by running `security find-identity -v -p codesigning` and `codesign` from the daemon's environment.

result.output:
The page doesn't explain the `errSecInternalComponent` or "unable to build chain" errors. It doesn't mention either message beyond a link title. What it does say is that the underlying problem is running code signing in a `launchd` daemon context. Quinn (Apple DTS) explains:

> A `launchd` daemon runs as root, and signing code as root is always problematic.

He also warns against a common workaround:

> using the `UserName` property in your `launchd` property list is not a good option, because it results in your daemon running in a mixed execution context.

**Recommended fix:** Run signing as a logged-in GUI user. Quinn lists three ways:

* Have the server auto-login as the GUI user and start your job runner in that context.
* Use screen sharing to start your job runner.
* SSH in to the machine and sign your code in that context. He calls this "the most practical" option.

For the `errSecInternalComponent` details, he points to a separate thread: [Resolving `errSecInternalComponent` errors during code signing](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/712005).

On the question of alternatives to `codesign`, Quinn says there are no supported alternatives. The on-disk signing format can change, and he doesn't support reverse-engineered approaches.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Turns OrcaSlicer's universal app into JusPrin.app and puts it in a disk image.
#
#   macos_package.sh <OrcaSlicer.app> <version> <output dir>
#
# OrcaSlicer's build names the bundle OrcaSlicer.app with OrcaSlicer's bundle
# identifier, icon and a "JusPrin <build id>" version string. This copies it to
# JusPrin.app and sets JusPrin's identity before anything is signed, because
# editing Info.plist afterwards would break the signature.
#
# Signing: with JUSPRIN_SIGN=1 the app and the disk image are signed with the
# Developer ID certificate in MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID (already in the keychain)
# and notarised with APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT, TEAM_ID and APP_PWD. Otherwise the app
# gets an ad-hoc signature, which keeps the edited bundle consistent but which
# Gatekeeper rejects for a download: that build is for testing only.
set -euo pipefail

source_app="$1"
version="$2"
out_dir="$3"

script_dir="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
repo_root="$(cd -- "${script_dir}/../../../../.." && pwd)"
entitlements="${repo_root}/scripts/disable_validation.entitlements"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${repo_root}/scripts/retry.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
stage="${work}/dmg"
app="${stage}/JusPrin.app"
dmg="${out_dir}/JusPrin_Mac_universal_V${version}.dmg"
mkdir -p "${stage}" "${out_dir}"
cp -R "${source_app}" "${app}"

plist="${app}/Contents/Info.plist"
buddy=/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy
set_key() {
    "${buddy}" -c "Set :$1 $2" "${plist}" 2>/dev/null || "${buddy}" -c "Add :$1 string $2" "${plist}"
}
set_key CFBundleIdentifier io.obico.jusprin
set_key CFBundleName JusPrin
set_key CFBundleDisplayName JusPrin
set_key CFBundleShortVersionString "${version}"
set_key CFBundleVersion "${version}"
set_key CFBundleGetInfoString "JusPrin ${version}"
cp "${repo_root}/resources/jusprin/images/JusPrin.icns" "${app}/Contents/Resources/images/JusPrin.icns"
set_key CFBundleIconFile images/JusPrin.icns
plutil -lint "${plist}"

if [ "${JUSPRIN_SIGN:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml signs: --deep misses the bundled Python
    # runtime, and notarisation rejects any Mach-O file without the hardened
    # runtime signature, so each one is signed, then the bundle last.
    # The main executable is left to the bundle's signature: signed on its
    # own, codesign checks the jusprin-mcp beside it, which the universal
    # join left unsigned, and fails with "code object is not signed at all".
    sign() {
        codesign --force --options runtime --timestamp --entitlements "${entitlements}" \
            --sign "${MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID}" "$@"
    }
    main_executable="${app}/Contents/MacOS/$("${buddy}" -c "Print :CFBundleExecutable" "${plist}")"
    machos=()
    while IFS= read -r f; do machos+=("$f"); done < <(
        find "${app}" -type f -print0 |
            xargs -0 file --no-pad --mime-type -- |
            grep -v ' (for architecture ' |
            grep ': application/x-mach-binary$' |
            sed 's|: application/x-mach-binary$||' |
            grep -vxF "${main_executable}"
    )
    echo "signing ${#machos[@]} Mach-O files in ${app}"
    sign "${machos[@]}"
    sign --verbose "${app}"
else
    codesign --deep --force --sign - "${app}"
fi
codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "${app}"

ln -sfn /Applications "${stage}/Applications"
retry hdiutil create -volname "JusPrin" -srcfolder "${stage}" -ov -format UDZO "${dmg}"

if [ "${JUSPRIN_SIGN:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    codesign --force --verbose --timestamp --sign "${MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID}" "${dmg}"
    notary=(--apple-id "${APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT}" --team-id "${TEAM_ID}" --password "${APP_PWD}")
    # notarytool exits 0 when Apple rejects the image, so read the status and
    # print Apple's report, which names each file it rejected.
    result="$(xcrun notarytool submit "${dmg}" "${notary[@]}" --wait --output-format json)"
    echo "${result}"
    if [ "$(plutil -extract status raw - <<<"${result}")" != "Accepted" ]; then
        xcrun notarytool log "$(plutil -extract id raw - <<<"${result}")" "${notary[@]}"
        exit 1
    fi
    retry xcrun stapler staple "${dmg}"
fi

rm -rf "${work}"
echo "${dmg}"

name: Mac signing test (temporary, never merged)

# Tries four ways to sign one small program with the Developer ID certificate
# on the self-hosted Mac, whose runner is a launchd daemon. Each prints OK or
# FAILED; the job itself only fails if none works.

on:
  push:
    branches: [claude/mac-signing-test]

jobs:
  sign:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, jusprin-release-mac]
    env:
      BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 }}
      P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.P12_PASSWORD }}
      KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
      MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
    steps:
      - name: Context
        run: |
          id; launchctl managername || true; echo "session: $(launchctl print gui/$(id -u) >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo gui || echo no-gui)"
          security list-keychains -d user; security default-keychain -d user || true

      - name: Try each way
        run: |
          set -u
          t="$RUNNER_TEMP"
          printf 'int main(void){return 0;}\n' > "$t/hello.c"
          clang -o "$t/hello" "$t/hello.c"
          cert="$t/cert.p12"; keychain="$t/test-signing.keychain-db"
          echo -n "$BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64" | base64 --decode --output "$cert"
          saved_list=$(security list-keychains -d user | xargs)
          saved_default=$(security default-keychain -d user | xargs)
          echo "$saved_list" > "$t/saved_list"; echo "$saved_default" > "$t/saved_default"

The page covers only part of your questions.

**Nested signing:** Yes, by default. The page says "we recursively sign entities by default," and that when you sign a bundle, it recursively signs "nested bundles/frameworks and Mach-O binaries inside that bundle unless told otherwise." It does not name dylibs, `.so` files, or specific paths like `Contents/MacOS` or `Resources`.

**Scoped settings:** The page says `rcodesign` has a settings mechanism that "allows you to scope settings to particular paths," down to individual Mach-O binaries within a universal binary. It gives no syntax for this. It doesn't mention `@main`, `@*`, or path-scoping syntax.

**`--code-signature-flags runtime`:** Shown only in the simple example for a Mach-O executable:

```
rcodesign sign \
  --p12-file developer-id.p12 --p12-password-file ~/.certificate-password \
  --code-signature-flags runtime \
  path/to/executable
```

The page doesn't explain how this option is scoped.

**`--entitlements-xml-file`:** Not mentioned.

**`--for-notarization`:** Not mentioned.

**DMG signing:** The page gives one example, using the same pattern as the bundle and executable examples:

```
rcodesign sign \
  --p12-file developer-id.p12 --p12-password-file ~/.certificate-password \
  path/to/app.dmg
```

It includes no DMG-specific options or behavior. A `.pkg` example uses `developer-id-installer.p12` instead.

cd /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/python-own-xz && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/macos_package.sh'
s=open(p).read()
old_hdr="""# Signing: with JUSPRIN_SIGN=1 the app and the disk image are signed with the
# Developer ID certificate in MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID (already in the keychain)
# and notarised with APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT, TEAM_ID and APP_PWD. Otherwise the app
# gets an ad-hoc signature, which keeps the edited bundle consistent but which
# Gatekeeper rejects for a download: that build is for testing only."""
new_hdr="""# Signing: with JUSPRIN_SIGN=1 the app and the disk image are signed by
# rcodesign (RCODESIGN) with the Developer ID certificate and key in the .p12
# file MACOS_P12_FILE, whose password is in the file MACOS_P12_PASSWORD_FILE,
# and notarised with APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT, TEAM_ID and APP_PWD. rcodesign reads
# the certificate itself, so no keychain is involved: Apple's codesign cannot
# use a keychain from a launchd daemon, such as the self-hosted Mac's runner,
# and fails there with errSecInternalComponent. Otherwise the app gets an
# ad-hoc signature, which keeps the edited bundle consistent but which
# Gatekeeper rejects for a download: that build is for testing only."""
assert old_hdr in s; s=s.replace(old_hdr,new_hdr)
old_sign="""    sign() {
        codesign --force --options runtime --timestamp --entitlements "${entitlements}" \\
            --sign "${MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID}" "$@"
    }"""
new_sign="""    # --for-notarization turns on the hardened runtime and Apple's time stamp.
    # Signing the bundle signs each file in it again, keeping the entitlements
    # each one was signed with.
    sign() {
        "${RCODESIGN}" sign --for-notarization --entitlements-xml-file "${entitlements}" \\
            --p12-file "${MACOS_P12_FILE}" --p12-password-file "${MACOS_P12_PASSWORD_FILE}" "$1"
    }"""
assert old_sign in s; s=s.replace(old_sign,new_sign)
old_loop="""    echo "signing ${#machos[@]} Mach-O files in ${app}"
    sign "${machos[@]}"
    sign --verbose "${app}\""""
new_loop="""    echo "signing ${#machos[@]} Mach-O files in ${app}"
    for f in "${machos[@]}"; do sign "$f"; done
    sign "${app}\""""
assert old_loop in s; s=s.replace(old_loop,new_loop)
old_dmg="""    codesign --force --verbose --timestamp --sign "${MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID}" "${dmg}\""""
new_dmg="""    "${RCODESIGN}" sign --p12-file "${MACOS_P12_FILE}" --p12-password-file "${MACOS_P12_PASSWORD_FILE}" "${dmg}"
    codesign --verify --verbose=2 "${dmg}\""""
assert old_dmg in s; s=s.replace(old_dmg,new_dmg)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

input.command:
sed -n 88,97p .github/workflows/jusprin_build_all.yml && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='.github/workflows/jusprin_build_all.yml'
s=open(p).read()
start=s.index("      - name: Load the signing certificate\n")
# include preceding comment block
cstart=s.rindex("\n\n",0,start)+2
end=s.index("      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7\n        with:\n          name: jusprin-macOS-universal")
new='''      # The app and the disk image are signed by rcodesign from the
      # certificate file itself (macos_package.sh): Apple's codesign cannot use
      # a keychain from the self-hosted Mac's runner, a launchd daemon, and
      # fails there with errSecInternalComponent. The certificate is the one,
      # under the secret names, that JusPrin 1.x used.
      - name: Get the signing certificate and rcodesign
        if: env.SIGN == '1'
        env:
          BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 }}
          P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.P12_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          umask 077
          echo -n "$BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64" | base64 --decode --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/signing.p12"
          printf '%s' "$P12_PASSWORD" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/signing.p12.password"
          rc=apple-codesign-0.29.0-macos-universal
          curl -sSfL -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/$rc.tar.gz" \\
            "https://github.com/indygreg/apple-platform-rs/releases/download/apple-codesign%2F0.29.0/$rc.tar.gz"
          echo "d98372d5524226ccf9dc0eda03d4e4f5826182dabb2fc3f2bd303ed9113a748d  $RUNNER_TEMP/$rc.tar.gz" | shasum -a 256 -c
          tar -xzf "$RUNNER_TEMP/$rc.tar.gz" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          echo "RCODESIGN=$RUNNER_TEMP/$rc/rcodesign" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Make the disk image
        env:
          JUSPRIN_SIGN: ${{ env.SIGN }}
          MACOS_P12_FILE: ${{ runner.temp }}/signing.p12
          MACOS_P12_PASSWORD_FILE: ${{ runner.temp }}/signing.p12.password
          APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT: ${{ secrets.APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT }}
          TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.TEAM_ID }}
          APP_PWD: ${{ secrets.APP_PWD }}
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/macos_package.sh \\
            build/universal/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app "$VERSION" dist

      # A self-hosted Mac keeps its runner's temporary folder between jobs.
      - name: Delete the signing certificate
        if: always() && env.SIGN == '1'
        run: rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/signing.p12" "$RUNNER_TEMP/signing.p12.password"

'''
s=s[:cstart]+new+s[end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
