git add deps/CMakeLists.txt deps/python3/python3.cmake deps/xz/xz.cmake && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Mac deps: give the bundled Python our own liblzma, and no Homebrew library

JusPrin 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 ship a Python whose _lzma module loads
/opt/homebrew/opt/xz/lib/liblzma.5.dylib, so `import lzma` fails on a
Mac without Homebrew. CPython's configure takes optional libraries from
whatever pkg-config finds, and GitHub's macOS images, like most
developers' Macs, have Homebrew's xz. On a Mac that also has Homebrew's
libb2, _blake2 loads that too.

- deps/xz/xz.cmake builds liblzma 5.8.4 as a static library (no tools,
  no docs), on macOS only. The archive's signature checks out against
  Lasse Collin's key.
- The macOS configure of the shipped Python now runs with
  PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR set to the deps' own pkg-config folders, so it finds
  that liblzma and nothing from Homebrew; _blake2 falls back to CPython's
  own BLAKE2 code. The x86_64 build's host Python, which only runs the
  build, is left as it was.

Built dep_python3 for arm64 and x86_64 on a Mac with Homebrew's xz,
libb2 and pkg-config on PATH: mac_outside_links.sh finds nothing in
either libpython, _lzma and _blake2 load only libSystem, an lzma
round-trip and blake2b work, and the module list matches the shipped
2.0.1 app (both lack only _gdbm).

Changing deps/ changes every platform's deps cache key, so the next
build on each platform builds its deps again, once.
EOF
git add .github/workflows/jusprin_build_all.yml src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/macos_package.sh && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Mac release: sign with rcodesign from the certificate file, not a keychain

On the self-hosted Mac, codesign failed with "unable to build chain to
self-signed root" and errSecInternalComponent even with Apple's Developer
ID intermediates in the signing keychain. A test job on that runner
reproduced it three ways: the keychain added to the search list, passed
with --keychain, and made the only and default keychain. The runner is a
launchd daemon with UserName set, and Apple's DTS says codesign does not
work reliably from that context (developer.apple.com/forums/thread/774832).
In the same job rcodesign 0.29.0 signed the same program, and codesign
--verify --strict accepted it: Developer ID Application, Developer ID
Certification Authority, Apple Root CA, with a secure time stamp.

rcodesign reads the certificate and key from the .p12 file itself, so the
universal job no longer creates, lists or deletes keychains, on GitHub's
Macs or on the self-hosted one. The p12 and its password are written to
the runner's temporary folder with umask 077 and deleted after the job.
rcodesign is the macOS universal release from GitHub, pinned by SHA-256
and itself signed with its author's Developer ID.

macos_package.sh signs each Mach-O file and then the bundle with
--for-notarization (hardened runtime, Apple's time stamp, and a check that
the certificate is Apple's Developer ID) and the same entitlements file,
and signs the disk image. Notarising is unchanged (notarytool).

Checked locally on a copy of the installed JusPrin.app with a self-signed
test certificate (--code-signature-flags runtime in place of
--for-notarization, which refuses a certificate Apple did not issue):
codesign --verify --deep --strict passes for the app and the disk image,
and all 72 Mach-O files carry the runtime flag, both entitlements and a
time stamp.

The secrets MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID and KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD are no longer read.
EOF
git add .github/workflows/jusprin_release_build.yml && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Release build: check every Mac app for libraries from outside macOS

mac_outside_links.sh ran only on the self-hosted Mac. GitHub's Macs have
Homebrew too, and 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 shipped a Python that loaded Homebrew's
liblzma from them. The check now runs after every Mac app build, so a
build that links Homebrew, MacPorts or XQuartz again fails instead of
shipping.
EOF

   - A static liblzma from xz 5.8.4, built with orcaslicer_add_cmake_project (deps/CMakeLists.txt helper).

     - `--entitlements-xml-file` is scoped to @main by default.
     - Re-signing a bundle keeps the settings already on the nested files.
   - mac_outside_links.sh: a check that lists every program or library loading a library from outside macOS.
   - GitHub workflows involved: jusprin_build_all.yml (the universal job, signing, the disk image), jusprin_release_build.yml (one platform), build_deps.yml (OrcaSlicer's upstream deps workflow).

I'd drop one of its commits, the one that loads Apple's intermediate certificates into a keychain, because rcodesign doesn't use a keychain. Links: [{"title":"Native matrix: macos-15 job not acquired by a hosted runner on the first scheduled run · Issue #116 · OpenCoven/coven-threads · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/OpenCoven/coven-threads/issues/116"},{"title":"CI: iOS qualification cannot acquire the hosted macOS 15 runner · Issue #700 · rgoza1996/Kinaiya · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/rgoza1996/Kinaiya/issues/700"},{"title":"CI: both macOS jobs use the scarce macos-15-intel runner, so fork runs fail with \"job was not acquired by Runner\" · Issue #189 · wf-group/wfview · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/wf-group/wfview/issues/189"},{"title":"CI: macOS job on macos-15-intel while arm64 runners take no jobs by sshlg · Pull Request #251 · passioncode-ai/passioncode · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/passioncode-ai/passioncode/pull/251"},{"title":"ci: macOS hosted-runner capacity shows up as abandoned legs and red batches · Issue #3124 · gerchowl/flock · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/gerchowl/flock/issues/3124"},{"title":"macos-15 jobs in this repository get no runner since 2026-11-16 12:29 UTC (blocks 0.1.9-lazurio.1) · Issue #218 · Lazurio/t3code · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/Lazurio/t3code/issues/218"},{"title":"Intermittent: webkit job: no hosted macOS runner acquired · Issue #489 · iwvelando/tangent-garden · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/iwvelando/tangent-garden/issues/489"},{"title":"fix(ci): main hosted runner acquisition failed after re2js bump in #103 · Issue #107 · lgtm-hq/bunq · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/lgtm-hq/bunq/issues/107"},{"title":"Track macOS hosted-runner capacity failures during release validation · Issue #400 · omniviewdev/omniview · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/omniviewdev/omniview/issues/400"},{"title":"[E002] CI iOS jobs on macos-15 get no runner and are cancelled after 15 minutes · Issue #413 · fivvi-app/fivvi · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/fivvi-app/fivvi/issues/413"}]

The search turned up many developer reports of this exact annotation on macOS 15 hosted runners, all from early-to-mid November 2026. None is an official GitHub statement, so the cause is inferred from the reports.

- **Cause:** Several reports attribute it to GitHub's hosted macOS capacity rather than the projects' own code. One issue notes that GitHub-hosted macOS arm64 jobs were repeatedly never acquired, and GitHub's accompanying notices say jobs targeting macOS arm64 runners may experience longer queue times.
- **Timing:** Reports range from 2 November 2026 ~18:55 UTC to 2026-11-18, run 44369702433. One repository reports that since 2026-11-16 12:29 UTC no macos-15 job in Lazurio/t3code has got a runner, while other repositories in the same organization were still getting runners.
- **Symptoms:** Jobs typically end as cancelled after about 15 minutes with no runner name and no steps executed.
- **Recovery:** Some jobs later succeeded on retry. For example, one project's previously cancelled macos-15 cells all ran and passed on a later attempt, and another acquired its macos-15 hosted runner and passed both actual iOS simulator app builds.
- **Workarounds discussed:** Projects have considered moving jobs to other macOS labels, such as arm64 images or an Intel label, though one report notes that GitHub Free allows at most 5 concurrent macOS jobs per account, which can also cause queuing.

If you need an authoritative answer, check GitHub's status page and the Actions documentation directly, since these results are third-party issue reports.

content.text:
The re-run on GitHub's own Macs failed the same way. GitHub cancelled it after 15 minutes because no hosted Mac took it. This isn't our build. Since 05:29 UTC today, no Mac job in this repository has got a hosted Mac, tonight's nightly builds included. Linux and Windows jobs still get machines.

What I checked:
- **GitHub's status page:** no open incidents, and Actions shows as working.
- **Billing:** the repository is public, so Mac minutes are free, and November's Actions bill nets to $0. No spending limit is blocking it.
- **Other jobs:** nothing else in the organisation is running or queued on a hosted Mac, so the free plan's limit of 5 Macs at once isn't the cause.
- **Other projects:** many report the same refusal on `macos-15` this month, some starting 16 November. Some got a machine on a later try. These are other projects' reports, not a statement from GitHub ([OpenCoven/coven-threads#116](https://github.com/OpenCoven/coven-threads/issues/116), [Lazurio/t3code#218](https://github.com/Lazurio/t3code/issues/218), [fivvi-app/fivvi#413](https://github.com/fivvi-app/fivvi/issues/413)).

`jusprin_release.yml` already notes that GitHub sometimes has no Mac free. A Mac release that depends only on GitHub's Macs can stall like this, and that's a reason to send releases to your Mac.

To get a hosted result anyway, I'm now trying two ways at once:
- The old `macos-15` run is retried as it was.
- A new run, 44594835461, uses `macos-26`, GitHub's current Apple-silicon Mac image, which also has Homebrew installed.

The `macos-26` switch is only on the temporary test branch, not in the fix. I also changed the self-hosted test so it no longer starts on every push, so your Mac isn't loaded again. When either hosted run produces a signed disk image, I'll check it the same way as your Mac's build.

Still open:
1. A passing build on GitHub's Macs, waiting on GitHub.
2. Landing. Nothing is on `jusprin-dev` yet.
3. The repository setting `JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER` doesn't exist yet, so releases won't use your Mac until it's set to `jusprin-release-mac`.
4. Deleting two unused secrets and my test branches after landing.
5. The runner session's question about running the runner inside a logged-in jusprin-ci session, which signing no longer needs.

Sources:
- [OpenCoven/coven-threads#116](https://github.com/OpenCoven/coven-threads/issues/116)
- [Lazurio/t3code#218](https://github.com/Lazurio/t3code/issues/218)
- [fivvi-app/fivvi#413](https://github.com/fivvi-app/fivvi/issues/413)
- [wf-group/wfview#189](https://github.com/wf-group/wfview/issues/189)
- [omniviewdev/omniview#400](https://github.com/omniviewdev/omniview/issues/400)
